# Wolfpack application

## When to read this
Read this for browser/PWA behavior, Bun HTTP/WebSocket or CLI behavior, session identity/control, Tailnet machine discovery, the durable task gateway, generated control-API contracts, or the TypeScript side of the broker boundary. Pair it with `broker.md` only when changing broker RPCs, PTY lifecycle, terminal snapshots, resize semantics, or output ordering. The Rust broker—not this module—owns PTYs and authoritative terminal state.

## Runtime authority and boundaries
The normal path is browser PWA → Bun HTTP/WebSocket server → per-user Unix socket → Rust broker → local PTYs. The Bun server owns API authentication, CORS/origin policy, project and command validation, session/task persistence, and translation to broker RPCs; it must not acquire a fallback PTY implementation (`src/server/index.ts`, `src/server/routes.ts`, `src/server/backend.ts`, `src/server/broker-backend.ts`). The browser is a renderer/controller. Terminal history and continuity come from broker snapshots plus sequenced output, never from browser caches.

The CLI owns setup, local configuration, service installation, upgrades, and scriptable control (`src/cli/`). Ordinary upgrades and setup changes restart only the server so broker-owned sessions survive. User configuration, session identities, task ledgers, and browser local state are separate persistence domains; preserve their validation, containment, permissions, and atomic/durable-write rules.

## Security and trust contracts
- Tailnet/global Wolfpack access is effectively shell-level authority over every visible session. JWT is optional and global; when configured it applies before protected API dispatch and WebSocket upgrade, but there is no per-session ACL (`src/auth.ts`, `src/server/index.ts`). An explicitly invalid secret is fatal before bind.
- Session creation validates project names/directories, harness/command shape, and initial prompts before executing local-user commands. Keep project containment in `src/server/validate-project-dir.ts`, command validation in `src/validation.ts`, and server-owned prompt delivery together.
- Public session projection must redact external-agent IDs. The broker UUID is durable session identity; names are collision-prone display selectors. Parent lineage is persisted separately and reconstructed across server restart (`src/server/session-identity.ts`, `src/server/persistence.ts`).
- Control API schemas publish compatibility, not authorization. Runtime route validation remains authoritative, and broker wire compatibility remains a separate Rust/TypeScript protocol contract (`src/control-api/schema.ts`, `src/server/routes.ts`).

## Tailnet control room and route authority
Setup persists `tailscaleHostname` only after structured `tailscale status` identity parsing and exact Tailscale Serve verification. The server derives sibling Tailnet CORS authority only from that canonical persisted hostname; request/forwarded headers cannot expand the allowed suffix. Serve may strip `Origin`, so HTTP recovery requires both Tailscale's injected login header and an allowed Referer (`src/cli/setup.ts`, `src/cli/tailscale-remote-setup.ts`, `src/server/tailnet-origin-policy.ts`).

`GET /api/tailnet/v1/candidates` returns only bounded, canonical facts from local Tailscale status; the server does not probe peers. The browser probes each candidate's public, no-store `GET /api/machine` directly with bounded body size, timeout, concurrency, redirects disabled, and credentials omitted. A peer becomes routable only when its handshake matches the candidate node ID/origin, supported protocol major, durable installation UUID, and required capabilities (`src/tailnet-machine-contract.ts`, `src/tailnet-peer-registry.ts`, `src/server/http.ts`).

Remote browser routes are keyed by `tailnetNodeId:installationId`, not stored URLs. Origins live only in the in-memory verified registry. Offline, malformed, removed, or enumeration-unavailable peers retain display diagnostics but lose route authority; an installation replacement revokes the old identity and retires affected terminals, grids, snapshots, and deep links. Notification links likewise carry stable machine identity and resolve it through the current registry (`public/app.ts`, `src/session-notification-route.ts`). `GET /api/discover` is only a deprecated online-candidate facade for compatibility.

## Broker integration, terminal attach, and recovery
`BackendRouter` owns the persistent broker client, startup handshake, timeout teardown, watchdog, and subscription preservation. `BrokerBackend` owns name-to-UUID caching and refcounted viewer subscriptions. Route callers decide whether an RPC is safe to retry; subscription failure or `replay_truncated` is a visual-consistency failure requiring a fresh snapshot (`src/server/backend.ts`, `src/server/broker-backend.ts`, `src/broker/client.ts`).

A browser attach settles dimensions, applies resize, waits for redraw quiescence, takes a broker snapshot, then streams ordered post-snapshot output (`src/server/websocket.ts`). One viewer controls a session; takeover displaces the prior viewer. Slow clients are closed at bounded queues rather than retaining unbounded terminal bytes. Prefill modes, chunking, `attach_ack`, `layout_stable`, `prefill_viewport`, `prefill_done`, `pty_ready`, close codes, and reconnect form one protocol across server and browser (`public/app.ts`, `public/app-grid.ts`, `src/ws-constants.ts`).

The browser registry is also a live route guard: remote REST and WebSocket construction must resolve a currently ready identity immediately before use. Do not reintroduce persisted/manual peer URLs. Grid and viewport attaches intentionally use bounded scrollback and shorter loading paths than full-terminal hydration.

## Session creation, status, and notifications
Top-level creation chooses a collision-resistant display name and retries only broker duplicate-name races; the returned broker UUID is durable identity. Child sessions carry parent identity without copying transcripts. CLI control should resolve UUID-aware selectors rather than infer identity from rendered names (`src/server/session-create.ts`, `src/server/session-open.ts`, `src/server/session-selector.ts`, `src/cli/session-control.ts`).

Agent runtime state and notification eligibility are server observations layered over broker sessions. Push enrollment is strictly same-origin, notification routes use stable session/machine identities, and stale peer identities must never turn back into origins through local storage (`src/server/agent-status.ts`, `src/server/session-observation.ts`, `src/server/push.ts`, `src/push-subscription-origin.ts`).

## Durable task gateway
`src/tasks/` is a server-owned durable Pi-task subsystem, not a broker protocol. `TaskGateway` validates participant sessions and transitions, serializes idempotency/delivery scopes, and projects local or direct-peer events. `TaskStore` uses append-only canonical JSONL ledgers, fsync/rename boundaries, rebuildable caches, quarantine, delivery sequences, tombstones, and retention cleanup; caches are never authoritative. Preserve immutable assignment hashes, participant checks, canonical event ordering, byte bounds, artifact containment, and crash-recovery behavior (`src/tasks/domain.ts`, `src/tasks/lifecycle.ts`, `src/tasks/store.ts`, `src/tasks/gateway.ts`).

Task federation currently addresses peers by canonical Tailnet HTTPS origin and is disabled when global JWT is configured. This is distinct from the browser control room's stable `nodeId:installationId` route identity; do not substitute one identifier contract for the other without a coordinated migration.

## Generated contracts and release pipeline
`src/control-api/schema.ts` is the source for `docs/generated/control-api.schema.json`; runtime behavior remains in routes/WebSocket handlers. Regenerate with `bun run gen:schema` and keep schema compatibility tests synchronized after public route/message changes. `scripts/build.ts`, `scripts/bundle-app.ts`, `scripts/gen-assets.ts`, and `src/public-assets.ts` package browser assets; audit source modules rather than generated bundles as independent implementations.
